Alinery is "a little bit like" what I'm doing with the design pattern cascades, insofar as it produces graphs that govern workflows and I similarly am creating graphs (or semilattices / CT diagrams) that act as "policies" that regulate workflows.  It's kind of the same thing with a different terminological paint job, but what's interesting about this is not just the similarity but the fact that I didn't see that many other people talking about similar things, whereas much of SF Tech Week was samey-samey.  As for Mastra, it is YC backed and very snazzy, but at least a lot of it is open source and it looks like they are solving some of the same problems as the War Machine, albeit in a different way.  So, my overall sense is that I have been coming at similar problems to SF folks, but with a much more theory-heavy approach (Category Theory & Active Inference) and that I want to be able to demonstrate what's good about my approach while learning from theirs.

evidence/body.hook: Joe 2026-09-25 direction: the outer loop (mission selection) should itself be a cascade, one global interpretation of Cascade Live over the portfolio, live, giving a way to get unstuck; cheap selection without constructing candidates per mission
evidence/body.name: outer-loop-as-cascade
evidence/body.body:
Joe, 2026-09-25 (~15:30Z), on H-G-target part 2: constructed candidates are on the fly per target at flight time, so initial mission selection cannot depend on them (else 343 constructions before one choice). The outer loop must supply a cheap selection, and his recent thinking is that the outer loop should itself be a cascade: one global interpretation over the portfolio (problem = the field at HEAD; patterns = step kinds read-criteria / ask-interpretation / construct / fly / defer, with guards on per-target facts and declared produces tokens; actions = (target, step)), scored by the same EFE machinery, with its rates measured from its own record, and "live" so it can get unstuck (ask/read steps have epistemic value when a fact is absent; guards stop repeats). claude-8 agreed and framed it as option (i) with inputs, subsuming option (ii) (E alone) as the no-data case; claude-10's seed-on-the-record requirement still applies.

**Why:** makes the outer loop one more cascade under PROOF-2a's clauses rather than an uncovered part; gives G at target grain for every feasible target from the first click.

**How to apply:** before wiring, a read-only discovery stating the outer cascade as an interpretation (problem, universe, patterns, which produces tokens exist at HEAD vs typed absent, zero-rate ranking on today's field, construction cost); claude-10 reads it before the read step is placed. Related: [[holes-closed-singly-before-any-flight]], [[every-written-mission-is-feasible]], [[compute-on-the-fly-never-refuse-missing-list]].

DECIDED 2026-09-25 ~23:45Z (Joe, verbatim): "the outer cascade should be based on Cascade Live. You found that Cascade Live itself is missing some data but in any case this gives us a direction to go in." Working definition: the cascade supplies the action set over the eligible field, claude-10's mixture law (futon2 d615d06e) the choice, the draw's seed on the record, step-outcome rates measured through measured-cell. Cascade Live's gaps (no excursion/ticket nodes; mission→pattern section unreadable at 5 s/page; no tensions; lineage unattributed) are row 1's precondition work on Cascade Live's side, not a reason to wait. Self-caused lineage exclusion still Joe's to decide.

RULED 2026-10-22 ~22:45Z (Joe, verbatim): "yes, the \"canonical G\" should be used in the outer loop. As I have said before the outer loop is really no different from the inner loop, it is similarly based on a cascade for example, and I don't see any reason why it should be treated differently from a G perspective. It's true that the cascade serves a different purpose and is constructed/selected/parameterised differently, but the mathematics involved should be pretty similar (and formally, the same)." Context: that night the live outer route (`outer_policy_objective/evaluate`) still scored policies with its own outcome-evidence G (Dirichlet posterior-predictive KL to C, Dirichlet ambiguity, categorical EIG, ln E), while the Lean canonical G (GOverCascades / compareAtHorizonN) was wired only on the reading-family route, which a sealed outer selection bypasses. **How to apply:** the outer selection is to be stated in Lean as compareAtHorizonN over outer cascades, its evidence entering as pattern θ counts (novelty) rather than as a separate G; do not propose a second G law for the outer loop.
